title: Word Frequencies

concept.title: Keys can be words
body: Counting words is counting numbers with a different kind of key. Split the line into words, add one to the counter of each word, then print the words in alphabetical order. In Python, strings compare by their letters in dictionary order, which is what `sorted` uses.
In C++ a `map<string, int>` keeps its keys sorted; in Java use a `TreeMap<String, Integer>`. Splitting a line on whitespace needs `stringstream` in C++ and `split("\\s+")` in Java.

statement: Given a line of text with words separated by one or more spaces, print every different word and how many times it occurs, in alphabetical order, one word per line.
inputFormat: A single line of lowercase words separated by spaces.
outputFormat: For each different word in alphabetical order, print the word and its count separated by a space.
constraints: The line has between 1 and 20000 characters and at least one word.
Each word has 1 to 10 lowercase letters.

examples.input: the cat and the hat and the bat

hints: Count every word with a map.
Print the keys in alphabetical order.

explanation: A map from word to count is filled while the line is split into words; its keys are then printed in sorted order.
solution.complexity: Time O(total length + d log d), space O(total length).
